definition: The needle or cannula did not deploy, deployed early, bent, kinked or was not inserted properly.
The pod or infusion set came off the body or was dislodged: adhesive failed, peeled, fell or was knocked off.
Battery depleting early, reaching ERI/end of life early, or an unexpected battery or longevity reading.
No identifiable failure mode (e.g. high blood glucose with no device problem named), insufficient information, or a reason outside this list.
The joint dislocated, subluxed or was unstable or lax; includes malposition or malalignment causing instability.
No identifiable failure mode, insufficient information, or a reason outside this list.
Infection around the hip or knee implant (periprosthetic joint infection): revision, spacer, irrigation and debridement, or antibiotics because of infection.
Pacing not reaching the heart: high or low impedance, loss of capture, high threshold, lead dislodgement or fracture, header or connection problem, no pacing.
No identifiable failure mode, insufficient information, revision for an unknown reason, or a reason outside this list (e.g. blood clots, literature summaries).
Pump or pod electronics: fault or error alarm, battery, button, display, power, software or app, controller or communication, overheating, motor or drive problem, missing history.
Pain, stiffness, arthrofibrosis or reduced range of motion with no more specific cause named.
An implant component (stem, liner, insert, post, shell, tray, head) broke, cracked, fractured or dissociated from its mating part, in or out of the patient.
Wear of bearing surfaces or a reaction to wear debris or metal: polyethylene wear, osteolysis, metallosis, adverse local tissue reaction, corrosion, elevated metal ions.
The implant came loose from bone or failed to grow into or fix to bone (aseptic loosening, lack of osseointegration, subsidence, migration).
Communication, interrogation, telemetry, programming, software or firmware problem, unexpected reset or back-up mode, wrong data or display.
Infection, pocket erosion, hematoma or sepsis related to the implant site.
Insulin flow blocked or delivered wrongly: occlusion alarm, blockage, under- or over-delivery, delivery stopped.
Insulin leaked from the pump, pod, reservoir or infusion site.
The device sensed the wrong signals: over-sensing, under-sensing, noise or artifact, leading to wrong pacing or inappropriate therapy.
A problem during surgery or handling before implantation: component would not seat or lock, difficult insertion, wrong size, packaging or sterility problem, trial or instrument issue.
The patient's bone around the implant fractured (periprosthetic fracture), e.g. femur, tibia, patella or acetabulum.
Skin reaction at the infusion site: irritation, rash, itching, redness, allergy or site infection.
